title: I have been working for the past 6 months, after hours, on a retro platform game made in Codex, the demo in now live on Steam!
author: AlonBo
selftext:
Hey everyone, I'm new here. I am an illustrator and animator, and always had a passion for games but no code knowledge of any kind. Through the years I built a few "games", never finished - using toold that didn't require code, like the ancient klik&Play, Blueprints in unreal and the likes.

I have a full time job, so not a lot of spare time, but I have been working on the past 6 monthes on the sort of game I always wanted to make. I'm still working on it, the game is not finished - but the demo is, and is now available on steam to try out!

About the game: It started as a simple experiment in Codex and ballooned into a full blown platform game. Art and code are all made with Codex, music with Suno, and some art with Gemini. A LOT of manual editing and fixing were done in Photoshop and After Effects.

The very first virsion of the game:

https://preview.redd.it/l4xoflzsu9nh1.png?width=2756&format=png&auto=webp&s=284e7a29040a682419aa6b7fdcf755fc8afca3a9

What the game looks like today:

https://preview.redd.it/ftxvsed1v9nh1.png?width=2698&format=png&auto=webp&s=5cd0c5480e773280a363f7b79b4a58020ead1606

The demo is available for Mac and PC and is free for everyone to try (and hopefully enjoy)

  
The full game is hopefully going to come out next year. 

  
I used Codex to upload the demo to Steam as I had no idea how to do it myself. I find it extremely useful, as it contains both code and the art generation in one place... simply amazing.

comments.author: BootstrapParadox1
comments.body: How easy is it to put a game on steam? Curious as I'm working on a game atm and looking of places to share it.

replies.author: Shppo
replies.body: easy but you have to pay 100$

replies.author: BootstrapParadox1
replies.body: So not for me then seeing as the game will be for free

replies.author: AlonBo
replies.body: Like u/Shppo said, it's easy - I just asked Codex to do it for me. It takes time, you have to wait for approval, but Codex basically does the whole thing for you. So easy.

replies.author: Shppo
replies.body: nice hahaha I'd say it's even easy without codex

comments.author: Nineneji
comments.body: Art and animation are beautiful! How did you animate it so well, what is the pipeline like? i know you said generated with Gemini and fixed in photoshop but did you rig it or use sprite sheets?

replies.author: AlonBo
replies.body:
Thsnk you! It's sprite sheet based. I generated the first image of every pose in Codex, then used Gemini to animate it (walking cycle, climbing, jimping and such). I then used After Effects to key the background from the Gemin video and turned that into sprite sheet frames, adjusted latet in Photoshop as a big sprite sheet.

No rig here. It's all generated.

comments.author: _DDark_
comments.body:
The cover/capsule art feels AI, especially since it has a pixelizer effect on it, while the game itself is not pixelized and the framing of the art itself as well. I would replace that. There are also some images like [this](https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/5158780/a67d3dd5e9c4d46ecdc6ca978ce0eae059b9c6aa/ss_a67d3dd5e9c4d46ecdc6ca978ce0eae059b9c6aa.1920x1080.jpg?t=1788416473) where the foreground feels completely disassociated from background. And you can't get lazy, you should regenerate those statues so that the angle proper front i.e profile shot. Make sure the ground and statue feels properly grounded. You can't just make ground by using those tileable flatly lit textures either. I would tweak these and ensure consistency throughout. 

Other than that, looks good. Reminds of Captain Claw for some reason. Actually Captain Claw is a good reference, check out how bg and fg are done there. Though the ground there is angled, so not a perfect reference. Just for bg and fg. I know I'm a bit critical, but you shouldn't put so much effort and then get lazy at the end dude. Wishlisted, all the best dude.
